snapshotNote: Snapshot 12:52 UTC, 13 minutes old · Sunday 07:05 Mexico City · nothing has kicked off on either side · Rico Dowdle cleared waivers unclaimed at 01:00 and is now a free agent · this is before the official inactive lists, so any call resting on a designation is provisional · this brief does not refresh on its own
sources: Built from 43 web calls (19 searches, 24 page fetches) · NFL.com, Giants.com, Commanders.com, AtlantaFalcons.com, FantasyPros, Pro Football Network, DraftKings Network, DraftSharks, Sports Illustrated/OnSI, Yahoo Sports, NBC Sports, CBS Sports, RotoWire, amNewYork, BlackAndTeal, Star Tribune, ESPN

tonight.headline: 0–0, 54%, and the honest answer this morning is that there is nothing to fire.
body: Neither side has a snap on the board. KEI returns set all nine slots overnight — Jaxson Dart, Achane, Skattebo, Drake London, George Pickens, Tyler Warren, the 49ers defence, McPherson and Parker Washington in the flex. Against a set lineup you are a 54% favourite on a projected 121.1 to 113.6. That is a coin flip with a lean.

You already made this morning's move: Michael Mayer out, T.J. Hockenson in at 06:26, exactly as the card said. Every remaining seat on this roster changed hands inside the last seven days, which closes them under the churn rule. There is no add, no drop and no lineup change to make before 11:00, and the two cards below are both marked do-not-fire on purpose.

case.label: Where the week is decided
case.body: Five of your nine starters play at 11:00 and two — Jonathan Taylor and Rashee Rice — do not kick off until 18:20 in the Kansas City game, which is also where KEI returns have nobody. Your quarterback slot locks at 14:05 when Jacksonville kick; that is the last decision of the day that is still yours.

case.label: What you executed
case.body: The Hockenson card fired seven hours ago at no priority cost. Bloodsports are still third of ten on waiver order with nothing spent all season, which in a league where priority never resets is the asset worth more than any of this week's moves.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Jonathan Taylor or Saquon Barkley appearing on an inactive list at 09:30 — that is the one branch that would open a closed seat and make Rico Dowdle, now a free agent, an immediate add rather than a Thursday one.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only — do not fire this
doFirst.title: Stafford in for Lawrence at quarterback — unarmed for a fourth run
doFirst.subtitle: Trevor Lawrence keeps slot 0. The projection gap is 2.6 points and the reporting gap is nothing; that is not enough to move a quarterback slot.

case.label: The case for Stafford
case.body: 17.4 against Lawrence's 14.8, at home against the Giants on Monday night, and Giants.com's own Week 2 preview calls him the reigning MVP and has all three of its analysts saying the Rams' offence is the bigger problem in that game than their defence. A 17.4 projection sitting on a bench in a one-quarterback league is a real cost.

case.label: The case for Lawrence
case.body: Yahoo's Jaguars-Broncos preview frames the game on protection rather than coverage: Lawrence averaged 3.12 seconds to throw in the last Denver meeting against Kansas City's 2.27, and the question is Anton Harrison against Nik Bonitto. Denver's corners are occupied outside — Surtain on Brian Thomas Jr., Riley Moss on Jakobi Meyers — which is where Lawrence's Week 1 profile lived: 11 of 13 on throws of 10-plus yards.

case.label: Why it stays unarmed
case.body: Two and a half points between quarterbacks two games into a season is inside the noise, and this seat has already been reversed once this week. STRATEGY section 3 is explicit that reversing a move made two days ago is never right. The correct answer to Stafford is the trade below, not the lineup.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Stafford outscores Lawrence on Monday night. That says the ESPN projection was the better instrument and this reversal was churn dressed as research — close it WRONG. Falsified early if Los Angeles put Stafford on an injury report, or if Jacksonville downgrade Lawrence before 20:05 UTC, which makes this card live.

doFirst.sources: Giants.com · Yahoo Sports · Sports Illustrated/OnSI · ESPN

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only — do not fire this
doFirst.title: Hockenson for Loveland at tight end — new, and unarmed from birth
doFirst.subtitle: Published so that the tight end you added this morning is a considered bench player rather than an unexamined one. Loveland keeps the slot.

case.label: Why the question exists at all
case.body: You now own both tight ends in the same game. Chicago and Minnesota kick off against each other at 11:00, and Colston Loveland's standing thesis falsifies itself in this exact game — 'fewer than four targets again in Week 2 against Minnesota'. Owning the other side of that is not a hedge you planned, but it is one you have.

case.label: The case for Hockenson
case.body: Minnesota are without Kyler Murray, ruled out with a concussion, and also without Jauan Jennings. Carson Wentz throwing to a thinned receiver room concentrates targets on Justin Jefferson and the tight end. Chicago's defence sits 14th of 32 on FantasyPros' Week 2 board at 8.23 projected points, in the tier the board itself labels 'surely you can find something better'.

case.label: Why Loveland keeps the slot
case.body: He projects 11.5 to Hockenson's 9.6, and STRATEGY section 10 forbids proposing a move worth under a point — this one is worth minus two. His role is also intact rather than lost: 65 snaps, 35 routes and 100% of Chicago's third downs in Week 1. What is missing is production, and production two games in is the noisiest thing on the page.

case.label: The number against him
case.body: Two targets in Week 1 and neither caught. Kalif Raymond led the Bears in targets, receptions and yards. SI's Week 2 piece is literally headlined that Loveland needs a much larger role, which is a way of saying he does not have one yet.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Loveland draws fewer than four targets again this afternoon. That is two weeks of a role problem no matchup grade survives, and the tight end slot changes hands on Thursday when his seat reopens — with Hockenson already on the roster, at no cost. Double-digit targets and this card is deleted and the Ferguson watch row closes with it.

doFirst.sources: Sports Illustrated/OnSI · FantasyPros · Star Tribune · CBS Sports · ESPN

whatWentWrong.title: You now carry two tight ends and no run has said which one starts
whatWentWrong.lead: Hockenson came in at 06:26 on a card about a seat, not about a player. Nobody then asked whether he is better than the tight end already in the lineup.

case.label: What happened
case.body: The Mayer-for-Hockenson card fired exactly as written and it was right: Brock Bowers practised, Mayer's reason for being here expires this week, and the best free agent in a league whose flex takes a tight end is a tight end. No priority was spent.

case.label: What was missed
case.body: The card stopped at the acquisition. Loveland and Hockenson play each other at 11:00, Loveland's own falsification clause resolves in that game, and the run that made the add did not publish a comparison between them. That is now the ghost card above.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Nothing today — Loveland keeps the slot on a two-point projection gap and an intact role. It changes Thursday, when his seat reopens and the replacement is already on the bench rather than on the wire.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loveland clearing double-digit targets against Minnesota, which makes the second tight end a luxury and frees that bench seat for Rico Dowdle.

whatWentWrong.title: Rico Dowdle cleared unclaimed at 01:00 and the reporting on him got better overnight
whatWentWrong.lead: This brief declined the claim and was right to. It also filed him as a Do-not-chase, and that half has not aged well.

case.label: What the decline was about
case.body: It was about price. In a league where waiver priority never resets, spending it on a committee back is what STRATEGY section 6 forbids outright. He cleared unclaimed, which is what the thesis predicted, and Bloodsports are still third of ten with nothing spent.

case.label: The number that changed
case.body: DraftSharks' Week 1 charting, read properly this morning: Dowdle took 58% of Pittsburgh's snaps, ran 20 routes to Jaylen Warren's 13, led early downs 25-17 and held third downs nine to two. In full PPR the third-down back is the one who pays. The Do-not-chase row was written against a player who does not exist.

case.label: Why he is still not an add today
case.body: The only seat he could take is Devaughn Vele's, and that seat changed hands on 17 September. STRATEGY section 3 closes a slot for seven days unless someone in it is ruled out. Vele is also a start today on his own merits — nine targets, seven catches, 69 and a touchdown in Week 1.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Thursday 24 September, when Vele's seat reopens, if Dowdle is still there — he is free to all ten managers, so he may not be. Immediately if Jonathan Taylor or Saquon Barkley is ruled out at 09:30, which meets the section 3 exception.

whatWentWrong.sources: DraftSharks · DraftKings Network · CBS Sports · ESPN

roster.footnote: Nothing has kicked off, so the right column is the matchup. Four tiles are dashed — Barkley, Loveland, Tuten and Lloyd — and each means I went looking this morning for a published read on that defence and came back without one, not that the matchup is average. Two games into a season a positional points-allowed rank is one game of data, so where reporting gave me something better it is in the detail line instead. This is a 07:00 run and the official inactive lists for the 11:00 games are not out yet.

starting.name: Trevor Lawrence
starting.detail: JAX · at DEN · SUN 14:05 · 11 of 13 on throws of 10-plus yards in Week 1. Yahoo's preview makes this a protection game — Anton Harrison against Nik Bonitto — rather than a coverage one. Locks first of your two quarterbacks.
starting.gradeEvidence: Denver's corners take both outside receivers — Surtain on Thomas, Moss on Meyers

starting.name: Jonathan Taylor
starting.detail: IND · at KC · SUN 18:20 · 22 touches for 121 yards and two scores in Week 1 while Indianapolis were thoroughly outplayed. Pro Football Network have him RB7 this week and say the floor is the role, not the matchup.
starting.gradeEvidence: Kansas City 5th of 32 on FantasyPros' Week 2 stream board

starting.name: Saquon Barkley
starting.detail: PHI · at TEN · SUN 11:00 · Philadelphia are FantasyPros' second-best defensive stream this week, which is another way of saying they are expected to lead — and a heavy favourite's back gets fourth-quarter carries. 26 touches in Week 1, with CBS reporting the Eagles intend to manage that number down.

starting.name: Rashee Rice
starting.detail: KC · vs IND · SUN 18:20 · two targets and seventeen targetless routes in Week 1 before turning a red-zone screen into a touchdown — an 8% target share, his lowest since his rookie year, with the slot rate down from 40%+ to 25%. Kansas City threw for 184 yards as a team. Off the injury report entirely.
starting.gradeEvidence: PFN have him WR8 this week; Indianapolis' Week 1 damage came against the run

starting.name: Garrett Wilson
starting.detail: NYJ · vs GB · SUN 11:00 · Geno Smith throwing — 19 of 24 for 215 in Week 1, his best since November 2025. Wilson led the Jets with seven targets and 79 yards.
starting.gradeEvidence: Green Bay outside FantasyPros' Week 2 top five; the board calls a bounce-back 'reasonable'

starting.name: Colston Loveland
starting.detail: CHI · vs MIN · SUN 11:00 · Caleb Williams throwing — two targets in Week 1 and neither completed, while Kalif Raymond led Chicago in targets, catches and yards. 65 snaps, 35 routes, 100% of third downs. The role is intact; the production is not, and this game settles it.

starting.name: Matthew Golden
starting.detail: GB · at NYJ · SUN 11:00 · Jordan Love throwing, and he threw 42 times to 21 handoffs in Week 1. Golden took a team-leading 30% target share — 12 targets, 6 for 95, two red-zone looks, 60 air yards. DraftKings' verdict is START.
starting.gradeEvidence: DraftKings: a middling Jets draw with a crack in it — Minkah Fitzpatrick doubtful

starting.name: Ravens D/ST
starting.detail: BAL · vs NO · SUN 11:00 · New Orleans gave up five sacks in the first half of Week 1 and threw two interceptions; Tyler Shough is throwing. Required weekly comparison, answered hold — and never with priority in this league.
starting.gradeEvidence: Baltimore 3rd of 32 on FantasyPros' Week 2 stream board

starting.name: Jason Myers
starting.detail: SEA · at ARI · 20:25 · held because the seat changed hands on 18 September, not because he is the best available. Cam Little K3, Will Reichard K5 and Chase McLaughlin K6 are all free agents here and all outrank him. The churn window expires 25 September.
starting.gradeEvidence: Pro Football Network final Week 2 kickers: Myers K9

bench.name: Matthew Stafford
bench.detail: LAR · vs NYG · MON 18:15 · a 17.4 projection that cannot enter a one-quarterback lineup. Giants.com's Week 2 preview calls him the reigning MVP and has its analysts naming the Rams' offence the bigger problem in that game. He is the trade chip below, not a lineup option.

bench.name: T.J. Hockenson
bench.detail: MIN · at CHI · SUN 11:00 · added at 06:26 this morning. Carson Wentz throwing — Kyler Murray ruled out with a concussion — and Minnesota are also without Jauan Jennings, which concentrates the targets on Jefferson and the tight end.
bench.gradeEvidence: Chicago 14th of 32, 8.23 projected — FantasyPros' 'find something better' tier

bench.name: MarShawn Lloyd
bench.detail: GB · at NYJ · SUN 11:00 · Josh Jacobs has been on the Commissioner's Exempt List since 30 August (NFL.com, ESPN, Packers News), so Green Bay's lead back is gone indefinitely and Lloyd is first on the depth chart. The cap is the offence, not the committee: Love threw 42 times to 21 handoffs in Week 1.

bench.name: Bhayshul Tuten
bench.detail: JAX · at DEN · SUN 14:05 · 48% of snaps, 52% of the carries, 36% of routes, no goal-line work; Chris Rodriguez Jr. took 41% of snaps and 40% of routes. He is the asset in the Lamar offer, so a big day here is not unambiguously good news.

bench.name: Devaughn Vele
bench.detail: NO · at BAL · SUN 11:00 · Tyler Shough throwing — five sacks and two interceptions in Week 1. Vele went 7 of 9 for 69 and a touchdown on a 17.3% share, second only to Chris Olave, who is questionable with a hamstring. DraftKings call him a start if you need a flex body, a floor play rather than a week-winner.
bench.gradeEvidence: Baltimore 3rd of 32 on FantasyPros' Week 2 stream board

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +40.6 across the season against your +11.6, and +2.5 a week on the lineup they actually have set — Tuten replaces Rachaad White, who they start at 7.6. Put that number in the message; it is the reason it gets read.

case.label: Their structural surplus
case.body: Re-verified against this morning's file rather than carried: Lamar Jackson sits at slot 20 behind Josh Allen at slot 0 in a one-quarterback league, so he scores Team 13 exactly zero every week. That is the surplus STRATEGY section 7 says to trade into. They also start Rachaad White at running back on a 7.6 projection, and Washington's Week 1 backfield snaps were Croskey-Merritt 33, White 27 — he is the second back in his own committee.

case.label: What you gain
case.body: Lamar 312.9 against the 286.4 your best quarterback currently projects, and Bhayshul Tuten leaves a bench where he is behind Taylor, Barkley and a flex that Golden occupies. In a ten-team league the roster spot you open is refillable from the wire and a top-two quarterback is not.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Both sides are priced on seasonProj, and seasonProj has returned identical figures on four snapshots. If it is a preseason artifact, this is trading on August's opinion and the real weekly gain is +3.4, which still clears STRATEGY's one-point floor but by much less than the headline. Tuten is also the only back on this roster who would start if Taylor or Barkley went down.

case.label: The better version if they counter
case.body: Matthew Golden for Lamar scores +26.5 to you and +12.2 to them — more than twice your gain on the Tuten version. It is not the offer that went out because it gives them a third of the upgrade and this manager has not responded to three offers. If they counter at all, that is the direction to push.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second real running back, which kills their +40.6. Or they trade or drop a quarterback, which kills the surplus. Or Lamar Jackson appears on a Baltimore injury report — he is not on this week's, checked again this morning. Or Rachaad White is dropped or benched by Team 13, which removes the evidence the offer is built on. Do not re-send; respond only if they open the conversation or counter.

trades.sources: ESPN · RotoWire · Davis Mattek snap charting · FantasyPros
trades.copyText: Hi — would you do Bhayshul Tuten for Lamar Jackson? You're carrying Lamar behind Josh Allen in a one-QB league, so he scores you nothing every week, and Tuten would go straight into your RB2 over Rachaad White (7.6 projected, and he was second in Washington's own backfield snaps in Week 1 — 33 to 27 behind Croskey-Merritt). By ESPN's season numbers that's about +40 for you and +12 for me. Happy to look at a different back on your side if Tuten isn't the one.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +15.5 across the season against your +4.7 — more than three times yours, because you are handing them a starting quarterback upgrade over Baker Mayfield and taking a receiver off their fifth bench slot.

case.label: Why it works for them
case.body: Metcalf Gala start Baker Mayfield at slot 0 on a 259.0 season projection. Stafford is 286.4 and Giants.com call him the reigning MVP. Waddle is at slot 20 behind Amon-Ra St. Brown, Mike Evans and Chris Olave in their flex — he is their fourth receiver and their surplus.

case.label: Why it works for you
case.body: Stafford cannot enter a one-quarterback lineup behind Trevor Lawrence and is worth exactly nothing to you on any Sunday. Waddle enters the RB/WR/TE flex and is worth +1.3 a week there on this week's numbers. Converting a dead bench slot into a live flex body is the whole trade.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Waddle is on Denver in this file, not Miami. A 214.3 season projection for a receiver in his first year in a new offence, two games in, is a weaker number than it looks, and I have not been able to price his role there from reporting. This clears the bar on a season horizon and only barely on a one-week one.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Metcalf Gala acquire or start a second quarterback, which removes the upgrade they are buying. Or Waddle draws fewer than five targets at Denver today — which says a receiver on a new team has not found a role and the 214.3 is describing one he does not have. Or seasonProj is confirmed frozen, which reduces this to the +1.3 weekly flex gain.

trades.copyText: Hi — interested in Matthew Stafford for Jaylen Waddle? You're starting Baker Mayfield and Stafford is a clear upgrade at the slot — ESPN has him about +15 on the season for you, against about +5 for me. Waddle is your fourth receiver behind St. Brown, Evans and Olave, and he'd go into my flex. Straight one-for-one, no hard feelings if it's a no.

worthALook.name: Rico Dowdle
worthALook.lead: Promoted off Do-not-chase. The decline was about the price; he cleared unclaimed at 01:00 and the price is now zero.

case.label: What the charting says
case.body: DraftSharks on Week 1: Dowdle took 58% of Pittsburgh's snaps, ran 20 routes to Jaylen Warren's 13, led early downs 25-17 and held third downs nine to two. He is the snap leader and the passing-down back in that backfield, which in full PPR is the half that pays.

case.label: What is against him
case.body: Warren out-targeted him six to two and took both short-yardage carries, and DraftSharks' own conclusion is that while the split holds, neither back is trustworthy beyond a low-end RB2. He would be your fourth running back behind Taylor, Barkley and Lloyd.

case.label: Why not now
case.body: The only seat available is Devaughn Vele's, taken on 17 September, and STRATEGY section 3 closes a slot for seven days unless someone in it is ruled out. Vele is also a start today on his own merits. He is a free agent, so nothing is spent by waiting — the only cost is another manager taking him first.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Thursday 24 September when Vele's seat reopens, if he is still available. Immediately if Jonathan Taylor or Saquon Barkley is ruled out at 09:30 — that is the section 3 exception and it fires without waiting.

worthALook.sources: DraftSharks · DraftKings Network · CBS Sports · ESPN

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: The highest receiver season projection on this wire, free, and today he draws the corner who is not Surtain.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: 182.4 season projection, 76.7% rostered nationally, free agent here — the why=OWNED band STRATEGY section 4 calls the strongest single wire signal in a shallow league. NBC Sports have the thumb cleared and he came off Jacksonville's injury report entirely.

case.label: Today's specific edge
case.body: Yahoo's Week 2 matchup preview has Patrick Surtain II on Brian Thomas Jr. and Riley Moss on Meyers. Denver's best corner is occupied elsewhere and Meyers gets the other side.

case.label: The Jacksonville problem
case.body: You already hold Trevor Lawrence and Bhayshul Tuten. Adding a third Jaguar concentrates a roster that STRATEGY section 8 already flags as exposed in week 7, when Jacksonville are on bye. If the Lamar trade lands, Tuten leaves and that objection halves.

case.label: When to act
case.body: A clean line at Denver today makes him an add on the first freed seat. A second week limited with the thumb, or fewer than five targets against a corner who is not Surtain, closes this row.

worthALook.sources: Yahoo Sports · NBC Sports · FantasyPros · ESPN

worthALook.name: Jake Ferguson
worthALook.lead: Still the best free agent tight end here, and now explicitly behind Hockenson rather than ahead of him.

case.label: Why he stayed on the list
case.body: 167.4 season projection at 81.2% national ownership, and he cleared waivers in this league unclaimed. In a league whose flex takes a tight end, a second startable one has real value — which is why the seat went to Hockenson this morning.

case.label: Why he is not the move
case.body: The seat that existed is filled. Ferguson would now have to displace Hockenson, who was added seven hours ago, which is the same-slot churn STRATEGY section 3 exists to stop. The ordering is recorded so the next run does not rediscover him as an opportunity.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens appearing on a Dallas injury report — Ferguson then becomes the best free agent in this league outright and the argument reopens on a different seat, not on Hockenson's.

doNotChase.name: Cam Little
doNotChase.lead: Ranked K3 this week, free, and still the wrong move — you dropped him two days ago.

case.label: The comparison, run every week
case.body: Pro Football Network's final Week 2 board: Brandon Aubrey K1, Cameron Dicker K2, Cam Little K3 on the Denver altitude, Tyler Loop K4, Will Reichard K5, Chase McLaughlin K6, Jason Myers K9. Little, Reichard and McLaughlin are all free agents here and all outrank the kicker you own. This is reported rather than buried because holding has to be a decision.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: You dropped Cam Little at 07:06 on 18 September to add Myers. STRATEGY section 3 says reversing a move made two days ago is never right, and it has cost this roster twice. The kicker seat has already changed hands three times in four days; a six-rank gain at kicker is worth well under a point a week and does not buy back a fourth.

case.label: The second reason
case.body: Little is a Jaguar. You already hold Lawrence and Tuten, and Jacksonville's week 7 bye is the hole STRATEGY section 8 names by name. Re-adding him rebuilds the concentration you spent a move removing.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Myers finishing outside the top twenty kickers today while Little or Reichard finish top five. The seat reopens on 25 September when the seven-day window actually expires, and the answer then is whoever tops that week's board — as a free agent, never as a claim.

doNotChase.name: Will Reichard
doNotChase.lead: K5 this week and free, and the same closed seat applies.

case.label: The case for him
case.body: Pro Football Network have Reichard K5 on long-range accuracy and Minnesota's indoor schedule. He is 29.8% rostered and free here, so no priority is at stake — only a roster move.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Four ranks above Jason Myers is worth a fraction of a point a week. STRATEGY section 10: do not propose a move worth under a point, and the transaction cost of being wrong exceeds the gain. He also plays at 11:00 today, so the window to act on this closes before the comparison can be tested.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Myers outside the top twenty this week while Reichard finishes top five. The seat reopens 25 September and the answer is whoever tops the board that week, as a free agent.

settled.title: Drop Michael Mayer for T.J. Hockenson when rosters unlocked (19–20 September)

settled.result: Cam Little K3 and Reichard K5 are both free and both better this week. The seat is still closed until 25 September and re-adding the kicker you dropped on Friday is the churn STRATEGY was written to stop.

settled.result: Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List, placed 30 August. The vacancy is intact and Lloyd is first on the depth chart.

settled.result: Re-scored this morning at +16.9 you, +21.8 them — the largest mutual-gain pair in the league and still not to be sent. Allen is Team 13's slot 0 and the consensus QB1.

settled.result: Still reversed, still a ghost, still unresolved until Monday night. Four runs on a 2.6-point quarterback gap is more attention than the question deserves.

settled.result: 65 snaps, 35 routes, 100% of third downs, two targets, neither caught. SI's Week 2 piece is headlined that he needs a much larger role. Today is the game that settles it.

cannotSee.body: The 11:00 games publish inactives around 09:30 your time. Everything resting on a designation — Chris Olave questionable, Brock Bowers doubtful, Josh Jacobs exempt, Kyler Murray out — is provisional. The one that would change a decision is Taylor or Barkley: either being ruled out opens a closed seat and makes Rico Dowdle an immediate add.

cannotSee.body: He is on Denver in this file, and the trade below is priced on a 214.3 season projection for a receiver in a new offence two games in. Four searches returned Miami-era material and nothing on his Denver target share. That offer is the weaker of the two and this is why.

cannotSee.body: seasonProj returned figures identical to earlier snapshots. Both trades above are priced partly on it. If it is a preseason artifact, the Lamar deal's real gain is the +3.4 weekly figure and the Waddle deal's is +1.3.

cannotSee.body: Tennessee against the run, Minnesota against tight ends, Denver against the run and the Giants' pass defence are the four I could not find a published Week 2 read for. The RotoBaller and FantasyPros pages that carry those numbers render their tables in widgets that do not come back as text.

cannotSee.body: Rashee Rice and Jonathan Taylor are both in that 18:20 game and both are in your starting lineup. I confirmed starters for Green Bay, the Jets, Chicago, Minnesota, New Orleans, Jacksonville, Baltimore and the Giants, and did not get a Week 2 confirmation for Kansas City or Indianapolis.

cannotSee.label: Rivals' pending waiver claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own. Rico Dowdle and Jakobi Meyers are free agents to all ten managers, so the Thursday plan for Dowdle is an instruction for a moment that may not exist.

cannotSee.label: Waiver priority is the asset this brief keeps refusing to spend
cannotSee.body: Third of ten, nothing spent all season, and it never resets. Every add this week has been a free agent. That is the correct use of section 6 and it is also the reason several of these rows say 'wait' where a Chem row would say 'claim'.
